lines.text: Cell Nine had no lock we could pick. Its door opened only to a Measurer's lens, held up to the eye carved in the iron.
The College gave me my lens back the day I reported in. Nobody ever thinks to watch a junior.
She held it up to the eye. The iron sighed, and the door swung in. Tamsin is very good at being underestimated.
Ilse sat on a stone bench in the dark, with her back very straight. Her grey dress was torn. Her wrists were bruised. She had no spectacles at all.
Lucan. I told you not to come.
You did. I'm a very bad listener.
You are. You always have been. Did anyone bring my glasses?
Tamsin had them in her pocket. Ilse's own, the round ones. She put them on, and blinked at us, and for a moment she couldn't speak.
Thank the gods. Everything down here has been a blur with opinions.
Then she held out her hands, and I took them. They were colder than mine. That had never happened before.
They put a stone on me for three days. They took a ring, Lucan. I'm a three now. It's very annoying.
She said it lightly. Her hands were shaking. Oswin put his cloak around her shoulders, over the torn dress, and nobody said anything about it.
And because she was Ilse, she had spent three days in a cell counting things.
Below us is a level they call the farm. The Measurers come back from it white and quiet. And below the farm, there is a room the Grand Measurer visits alone. Every night.
Maric's cure is pure hollow-born aether. There is only one place in Aldmere that can come from. Down there.
Then we go down.
Of course we do. You've come this far without a single sensible idea. Why start now?
On the way to the stair, she stopped at a door I hadn't noticed. Plain stone, with no handle, its edges sealed with lead.
Every Measurer is taught that the first Stone lies behind this door. The very Stone King Aldric touched, when he lit seven rings. Only the Grand Measurer may open it.
I have wanted to see it my whole life.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-eight, coming soon.
